In contrast, `found` and `price_stats` must reflect ALL active filters combined. - `facet_query` performs a case-insensitive prefix match over a field\'s facet values; use it to power the facet search box. - `max_facet_values` caps how many facet values are returned for each field. Request object (stdin): ```json {   "q": "*",   "filters": {     "brand": ["Apple"],     "category": ["Laptops"],     "tags": ["premium"],     "price": { "min": 500, "max": 2000 }   },   "facet_query": { "field": "brand", "prefix": "sa" },   "max_facet_values": 10 } ``` - `q` is optional and defaults to `"*"` (match all). When `q` is not `"*"`, search against `product_name`. - `filters` is optional. Any of `brand`, `category`, `tags` may be provided as a list of selected values (a document matches a field\'s filter if it equals any selected value). `price` is optional and given as an object with numeric `min` and/or `max` (inclusive bounds). - `facet_query` is optional. - `max_facet_values` is optional and defaults to `10`.  Response object (stdout): ```json {   "found": 6,   "facets": {     "brand": [ { "value": "Apple", "count": 2 } ],     "category": [ { "value": "Laptops", "count": 6 } ],     "tags": [ { "value": "premium", "count": 4 } ]   },   "price_stats": { "min": 599.0, "max": 1999.0, "avg": 1199.0, "sum": 7194.0 },   "facet_query_matches": [ { "value": "Samsung", "count": 3 } ] } ``` - `found` is the number of products matching `q` and ALL active filters. - `facets` must include the keys `brand`, `category`, and `tags`; each maps to a list of `{ "value": <string>, "count": <integer> }` objects sorted by `count` in descending order, following the disjunctive semantics described above. - `price_stats` must contain the numeric keys `min`, `max`, `avg`, and `sum`, computed over the products matching `q` and ALL active filters, each rounded to 2 decimal places. If no products match, use `0` for every statistic. - `facet_query_matches` must be present only when `facet_query` is supplied; it lists the `{ "value", "count" }` matches (case-insensitive prefix) for the requested field under the current active filters, sorted by `count` descending.                       [32m'Build a tiny catalog, index it in Typesense, and learn to combine typo-tolerant q, filter_by, facet_by and facet_query_num_typos so misspelled searches still return correct, ranked results.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'So, we reset the collection and define the fields we will filter and facet on.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Facet by requests\n'[39m +

                      [32m'The facets\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{ts:289} comprehension normalizes the API response, making it easy to compare buckets downstream, lowering the price\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This example keeps typo tolerant facet refinement active in typesense when filters are stacked.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{ts:328} Users often misspell facet values like shoe.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'Typesense gives you typo tolerant queries plus correct\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{ts:389} faceting on the same index.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Use this when your users spell things unpredictably but still need accurate'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# What and how do I perform a search operation in ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2022-05-04, last updated: 2025-09-13, [Read more](https://dev.to/aviyel/what-and-how-do-i-perform-a-search-operation-in-typesense-5gc5)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'A search in Typesense consists of a query against one or more text fields, as well as a set of filters against numerical or facet fields.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can sort and facet your results as well.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- facet_by: facet_by will help you facet your results.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Don't forget to use a comma to separate multiple fields.\n"[39m +

                      [32m'- facet_query: This parameter can be used to filter the facets that are returned.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# MultiSearchCollectionParameters in typesense_rs::models\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-05-05, [Read more](https://docs.rs/typesense-rs/latest/typesense_rs/models/multi_search_collection_parameters/struct.MultiSearchCollectionParameters.html)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'pub facet_by: Option<String>,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'pub facet_query: Option<String>,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'pub facet_return_parent: Option<String>,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'§`facet_by: Option<String>`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'A list of fields that will be used for faceting your results on.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Separate multiple fields with a comma.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'§`facet_query: Option<String>`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Facet values that are returned can now be filtered via this parameter.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The matching facet text is also highlighted.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For example, when faceting\n'[39m +

                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Hello, Is it possible to search facets? My structure is\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2024-07-07, last updated: 2025-09-24, [Read more](https://threads.typesense.org/t/29444703/hello-is-it-possible-to-search-facets-my-structure-is-attrib)\n'[39m +

                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Typesense Search FAQs\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-04, [Read more](https://typesense.org/docs/guide/faqs.html)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Faceting - How do I get facet counts for values that users have not filtered on?\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You want to set `drop_tokens_threshold: 0` as a search parameter.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# How to retrieve available facet/filter options · Issue #66 · typesense/typesense\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2019-06-08, last updated: 2026-04-16, [Read more](https://github.com/typesense/typesense/issues/66)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To filter without a specific item, you will remove that item from the filter items and run the filter again.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"For example, let's say you are filtering with `product_type: [X, Y, Z]` and now want to filter without `Y`, then you just do `product_type: [X, Z]`.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For this you can use the `facet_by` option.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'See the description for the `facet_by` argument here.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In this case, you will do something like:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m"client.collections['products'].documents.search({\n"[39m +
                      [32m"'q': 'apple',\n"[39m +
                      [32m"'query_by': 'title, product_type, brand',\n"[39m +
                      [32m"'filter_by': '[product_type: mobile, computer, accessories]'\n"[39m +
                      [32m"'facet_by': 'brand, product_type'\n"[39m +
                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This would return the brands and product types present in the search results, along with their respective counts.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Check the `facet_counts` field in the response to get those values.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Using `facet_by` is the correct way to enumerate the unique categories present in a search result.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Currently, the counts returned by the `facet_by` response is limited to the top 10 frequently occurring entities.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Collections | Typesense\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2021-10-12, last updated: 2026-06-19, [Read more](https://typesense.org/docs/0.21.0/api/collections.html)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|Parameter|Required|Description|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|name|yes|Name of the collection you wish to create.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|fields|yes|A list of fields that you wish to index for querying, filtering and faceting.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For each field, you have to specify the `name` and `type`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**Declaring a field as optional** A field can be declared as optional by setting `"optional": true`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**Declaring a field as a facet** A field can be declared as a facetable field by setting `"facet": true`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Faceted fields are indexed verbatim without any tokenization or preprocessing.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For example, if you are building a product search, `color` and `brand` could be defined as facet fields.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'However, you can still explicitly define specific fields (with or without RegEx names) to facet by\n'[39m +
                      [32m'setting `facet: true` for them.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For e.g. `{"name": ".*_facet", "facet": true" }`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This will only set field names that end with `_facet` in the document, as a facet.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Retrieve the details of a collection, given its name.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'#### # Definition\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`GET ${TYPESENSE_HOST}/collections/:collection`'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Build a Search Application with Typesense\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-07, [Read more](https://typesense.org/docs/guide/building-a-search-application.html)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For each field, we define its\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'facet\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'field.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'A facet field allows us to cluster the search results into categories and lets us drill into each of those categories.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'We will be seeing faceted results in action at the end of this guide.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In this case, books that have more ratings will be ranked higher.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You only need to include fields that you want to search / filter / facet / sort / group_by in the collection schema.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'We call these indexed fields.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"We will start with a really simple search query - let's search for\n"[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'harry potter\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Now, let's tweak our query to only fetch books that are published before the year 1998.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'To do that, we just have to add a\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'filter_by\n'[39m +

                      [32m'clause to our query:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## # Faceting\n'[39m +

                value: [
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Typesense filter_by Syntax and Examples\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-07-30, last updated: 2026-08-07, [Read more](https://typesense.org/docs/guide/tips-for-filtering.html)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can\n'[39m +
                      [32m'use the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'filter_by\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'parameter to specify a custom filter string.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"q": "*",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// ...Note that the base format for a filter is\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'field: <operator> <value>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'. Every filter field must have\n'[39m +
                      [32m'a ** after it. :**- ✅ Correct:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Commas act as OR operators, allowing flexible condition combinations.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For example, to filter for products that are either made in the USA or Canada, and are located in New York, you can use the following filter:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'(country:=USA || country:=Canada) && city:=New York\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When filtering on fields inside nested array objects, you need to use a special syntax to ensure the filters are applied to the same object within the array. The syntax is:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'<nested_field_parent>.{<filter_conditions>}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# Find dishes with either high cheese concentration or jalepeno\n'[39m +
                      [32m'filter_by=ingredients.{name:=cheese && concentration:>50} || ingredients.{name:=jalepeno}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# Find dishes with cheese concentration between 30 and 50\n'[39m +
                      [32m'filter_by=ingredients.{name:=cheese && concentration:[30..50]}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Typesense Search API Parameters\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-02, [Read more](https://typesense.org/docs/30.2/api/search.html)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|Parameter|Required|Description|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|query_by|yes|One or more field names that should be queried against.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Separate multiple fields with a comma: `company_name, country`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The order of the fields is important: a record that matches on a field earlier in the list is considered more relevant than a record matched on a field later in the list.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'So, in the example above, documents that match on the `company_name` field are ranked above documents matched on the `country` field.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Only string and string array fields can be used for full-text search in the query_by parameter.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"When you specify an object or object array field, Typesense uses the object(s)' children's string and string array fields automatically.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|Parameter|Required|Description|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can use the `filter_by` search parameter to filter results by a particular value(s) or logical expressions.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For eg: if you have dataset of movies, you can apply a filter to only return movies in a certain genre or published after a certain date, etc.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'$<collection>(<facet_field1>, <facet_field2>, ...)'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Boolean Search with Tags\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-07-30, last updated: 2026-07-14, [Read more](https://typesense.org/docs/guide/boolean-tag-search.html)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Typesense supports boolean queries like this when filtering, using the `filter_by` property.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"We'll create a function that converts tags with field types into Typesense filter syntax.\n"[39m +
                      [32m"For array fields like genres, we'll use the `:` operator, and for string fields like title, we'll use `:=` for exact matching.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'This is the part of the code where we construct our boolean search expression.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In our case we are OR-ing all values of the same field type into a shared clause, and AND-ing all of those clauses together.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'But this logic could be any valid boolean equation, as defined by the filter_by docs here (opens new window)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'if (filters.length === 0) return null;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Join multiple values with OR\n'[39m +
                      [32m"return filters.length === 1 ? filters[0] : `(${filters.join(' || ')})`;\n"[39m +
                      [32m'}).filter(f => f !== null);\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Join different field types with AND\n'[39m +
                      [32m"return fieldFilters.join(' && ');\n"[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'function escapeFilterValue(value) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m`return value.replace(/"/g, '\\\\"');\n`[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This allows us to handle multiple queries and union the results together, which allows us to get OR logic when we have multiple "all fields" tags.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Typesense Search FAQs\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-04, [Read more](https://typesense.org/docs/guide/faqs.html)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If you need to do more structured queries, then you can use the `filter_by` search parameter, which supports complex boolean expressions with precedence, etc.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"For eg, let's say we want to search for `software engineering lead` OR `software engineering manager` in the same search query.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'You could do something like this:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"q": "*",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"filter_by": "job_title:[software engineering lead, software engineering manager]"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"q": "*",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"filter_by": "job_title:software engineering lead && job_location:[remote, hybrid]"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"q": "*",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"filter_by": "job_title:=software*"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"q": "shoes",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"filter_by": "category:=Athletic",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"max_candidates": 100\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# search: OR("||") operator support in filter_by clause · Issue #281 · typesense/typesense\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2021-06-01, last updated: 2026-04-17, [Read more](https://github.com/typesense/typesense/issues/281)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`filter_by` currently only supports `OR`ing values in the same field, and `AND`ing values across fields or the same field.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If you need to `OR` across fields, the work-around would be to send multiple queries using the `multi_search` endpoint, with each query having a particular field in the `filter_by` expression and then aggregating the results client-side for these queries.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"There's a `_text_match` score as part of each `hits` hash that can be used for this cross-collection aggregation.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"We've added a `||` operator for doing ORs.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'So, you can now do something like: `grade:>10 || is_premier: true`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This build also supported nested filtered expressions, e.g. `(grade:>10 || is_premier: true) && gender:=Female`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Yes, nested filter expressions are supported in this build as well.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`(grade_math:=1 || grade_english:=2)` filter says: fetch a record that has either `grade_math: 1` or `grade_english: 2`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To achieve what you want, you need to have: `(grade_math:=1 && grade_english:=2)`.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m"# Typesense 'OR' query mode\n"[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2022-02-18, last updated: 2025-03-12, [Read more](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/71172284/typesense-or-query-mode)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Typesense doesn't support strict ORs and currently have no plan to do so.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'To solve my problem I used\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`filter_by`instead like so:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This would return all products of category shoe/hat/dress/parfume.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'I recommend to use embedding and then sending "show hat dress perfume" in the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`q`query.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Typesense OR query on multiple fields\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2022-10-12, last updated: 2025-05-30, [Read more](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/74036058/typesense-or-query-on-multiple-fields)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can accomplish this with comma-separated fields instead of using multi-search.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'I.e.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{query_by: "message_from,message_to", ...}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- No need to use\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  filter_by\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  ```\n'[39m +
                      [32m', since you can just specify\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m"  {'q': 'abc', query_by: 'message_from,message_to'}\n"[39m +
                      [32m'  ```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'– Nathan Gould\n'[39m +

                    text: [32m'# ANTLR4 grammar for filter expression · Issue #396 · typesense/typesense\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2021-10-03, last updated: 2026-04-16, [Read more](https://github.com/typesense/typesense/issues/396)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Typesense currently supports a simple `filter_by` syntax that can do ANDs between different fields, but does not support ORs between fields or compound filter conditions.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'We want to support advance filtering operations and that requires generating a grammar for the existing filter syntax and extending it to support ORs (via `||`) and compound expressions.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Existing syntax\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# Filtering a single value\n'[39m +
                      [32m'name: Steve Smith\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# Filtering multiple values of the same field (we do an OR)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'name: [Steve Smith, `Jack & Jill`]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'age: [10, 15]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# Numerical comparators (we support <, >, <=, >= and ..)\n'[39m +

                      [32m'age: [>=10, 20]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'age:[10..100]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'We now want to support compound filters and `||` (OR) conditions.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Example:\n'[39m +

                    text: [32m'# Filter: Add `IN[]` operator · meilisearch · Discussion #479\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'I propose the following syntax:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'in_filter = value "IN" "[" value_list "]"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'value_list = (value ("," value)* ","?)?\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`IN[...]` selects all documents whose attribute contains at least one of the values given inside the brackets.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In case there are no values, then the filter selects no documents.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`NOT colour IN[...]` selects all documents with a `colour` attribute which contains values that are all different from those in the brackets.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Futhermore, square brackets denote lists in JSON and other programming languages, so it makes sense to use them here when we expect a list of values.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                      [32m'> Examples:\n'[39m +

                      [32m'> - `country: [USA, UK]` returns documents that have `country` of `USA` OR `UK`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The syntax is therefore similar but a colon is used instead of `IN`.\n'[39m +

          name: [32m'newTask'[39m,

            [32m'When using the newTask tool, the agentType parameter is optional. Leave it empty (None) to launch a generic sub agent, or specify one of the available agent types below to select a specialized agent.\n'[39m +
            [32m'Available agent types and the tools they have access to:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### browser\n'[39m +
            [32m'Web browser automation agent for navigating websites, interacting with pages, and extracting information. Uses agent-browser CLI for browser control, including headless sessions and optional local Chrome auto-connect.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### explore\n'[39m +
            [32m'Use this agent to explore the codebase when you need to: understand project structure, find where features are implemented, locate specific functions or classes, analyze code patterns, investigate how something works, search for examples or usage, or gather information before making changes.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of questions this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "where is the authentication logic implemented"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "find all usages of the config parser"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "how does the ignore-walk module work"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### guide\n'[39m +
            [32m"A comprehensive guide for learning about Pochi's capabilities, features, and configuration.\n"[39m +
            [32m'This agent helps users understand how to use Pochi effectively, fetch documentation, and modify their config file (.pochi/config.jsonc) with proper confirmation.\n'[39m +
            [32m"**IMPORTANT: Any request to modify Pochi's configuration must be handled by this agent.**\n"[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Trigger examples:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- General info: "what can Pochi do?", "what agents/tools are available?", "how does Pochi work?"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Configuration: "how do I configure Pochi?", "explain config options", "help me modify my config", "set up a new provider", "add an MCP server"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Help & feedback: "join the discord", "report a bug", "where can I get help?"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### planner\n'[39m +
            [32m'Engage this agent to formulate comprehensive, technical implementation strategies for feature development, system refactoring, or defect resolution.\n'[39m +
            [32m'This agent is strictly limited to planning and architectural design; it DOES NOT execute code modifications.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of user requests this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "create a plan to implement the user authentication feature"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "how should we refactor the database schema"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "design a solution for the memory leak issue"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'Engage this agent to perform code reviews and leave inline comments.\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of user requests this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +

            [32m'- "check this code and leave feedback"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Always include a reminder in your prompt to ensure the result will be submitted through the `attemptCompletion` tool.\n'[39m +
            [32m'If the task stops without submitting the result, it will return an error message.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'When NOT to use the newTask tool:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- If you want to read a specific file path, use the readFile or globFiles tool instead of the newTask tool, to find the match more quickly\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Usage notes:\n'[39m +

            [32m'2. When the agent is done, it will return a single message back to you. The result returned by the agent is not visible to the user. To show the user the result, you should send a text message back to the user with a concise summary of the result.\n'[39m +
            [32m'3. Each agent invocation is stateless. You will not be able to send additional messages to the agent, nor will the agent be able to communicate with you outside of its final report.
